drhp.business: The Company manufactures metallic card clothing and non-woven wires used in the carding process of textile spinning, along with machines for mounting, maintenance and servicing of card clothing, and provides technical servicing to textile mills. It also has an international presence in the non-woven business through operations in Turkey and its relationship with subsidiary Garnett Wire Limited, UK.

drhp.expansion: The Company commissioned a 0.56 MW (560 kW) rooftop solar power plant at its Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh factory during the year, aimed at enhancing energy efficiency and reducing carbon emissions. The Board approved a further investment of £250,000 in the equity share capital of subsidiary Garnett Wire Ltd., UK, in view of growing business opportunities for the Non-Woven business segment in India and overseas markets. The Company completed the sale of its commercial property at Baner, Pune, in July 2026.

risks.note: Demand for card clothing in the re-clothing market depends on carding-machine operating capacity, production rate, machine utilisation and fibre mix; a prolonged slowdown in textile and apparel demand can lower spinning-mill utilisation and cause postponement of card re-clothing.
The Company is exposed to volatility in the prices and availability of critical raw materials, particularly high-carbon and alloy steels, much of which is import-dependent.
Regulatory requirements relating to quality standards and imports of specialised alloy and high-carbon steel may affect procurement costs and lead times.
The Company is exposed to foreign-exchange fluctuations from its international operations and import of certain raw materials, which can affect export realisations and input costs.
Geopolitical developments, trade restrictions, tariff changes, international freight costs and economic conditions in major export markets may impact the Company's international business.

Increasing competition from Chinese manufacturers, particularly in price-sensitive markets, is a concern; card clothing manufacturers associated with carding machine OEMs may also have an advantage in initial replacement cycles of new machines.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Demand for card clothing in the re-clothing market depends on carding-machine operating capacity, production rate, machine utilisation and fibre mix; a prolonged slowdown in textile and apparel demand can lower spinning-mill utilisation and cause postponement of card re-clothing.
- The Company is exposed to volatility in the prices and availability of critical raw materials, particularly high-carbon and alloy steels, much of which is import-dependent.
- Regulatory requirements relating to quality standards and imports of specialised alloy and high-carbon steel may affect procurement costs and lead times.
- The Company is exposed to foreign-exchange fluctuations from its international operations and import of certain raw materials, which can affect export realisations and input costs.
- Geopolitical developments, trade restrictions, tariff changes, international freight costs and economic conditions in major export markets may impact the Company's international business.
- Increasing competition from Chinese manufacturers, particularly in price-sensitive markets, is a concern; card clothing manufacturers associated with carding machine OEMs may also have an advantage in initial replacement cycles of new machines.
- Increasing use of synthetic, recycled and blended fibres requires continuous development of specialised card clothing products and technical expertise, creating a risk of product obsolescence if the Company does not keep pace.
- Fluctuations in energy costs, labour costs, interest rates, taxation, natural disasters and supply-chain disruptions can adversely affect manufacturing costs and margins.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Increase market penetration in high-speed and high-production carding applications.
- Strengthen presence in the non-woven and technical textile sectors.
- Develop specialised card clothing for new and difficult-to-process fibres.
- Expand international business through existing sales and service infrastructure.
- Strengthen presence in international markets.
- Increase customer engagement through technical service and application support.
- Improve manufacturing productivity and cost competitiveness.
- Continue investment in product development and innovation.
